KPDP Marriage Matching Rules: Theory 
and Practice 


By: Tin Win 
Email: tw853@yahoo.com 





KPDP Marriage Matching Rules 


1. The Krishnamurthi Padhdhathi Dasavida Prorutham (KPDP) rules for matching of horo- 
scopes for marriage, framed by Shri K.P. Kuppu Ganapathi, cover 10 matching criteria 
which are to check as follows: 


KPDP No. 1: Characteristic compatibility 
Ascendant sub lords in the charts of the boy and the girl should be natural friends or 
equals, and should not be natural enemies. 


KPDP No. 2: Harmony in married life 
Ascendant sub lords and the 7th cusp sub lords in the respective charts of the boy and the 
girl should be should be natural friends or equals, and should not be natural enemies. 


KPDP No. 3: Attitudes and urges 
The Ascendant signs of the boy and the girl should be compatible, i.e., fire and fire, water 
and water, fire and air, water and earth, and air and water. 


KPDP No. 4: General happiness 

Work out the aspects under the Western system of aspects taking into account the pre- 
scribed orbs of the planets, between the Ascendant sign lords of the boy and the girl in their 
respective charts. They should form favourable aspects - otherwise no marks to be awarded. 


KPDP No. 5: Mutual understanding between the couples 


© Work out the aspects formed (by taking into account the orb of the respective planets) 
between the 7th cusp sub lords of the boy and the girl, in their respective charts. 

® See where the 7th cusp sub lord in the girl's chart is occupying in her chart. Similarly 
find out the placement of the 7th cusp sub lord in the boy's chart and work out the as- 
pect formed between these two by taking into account the orbs of the respective planets. 


Depending on the nature of aspect i.e., favourable or unfavourable, in respect of (i) and (ii) 
above give marks proportionately. 


KPDP No. 6: Pleasure and happiness after marriage 
Birth star lord of the boy should occupy houses 2, 3, 5, 7, 9 or 11 in the girl's chart and vice 
-versa. 


KPDP No. 7: General suitability for marriage 

7th cusp sign, star and sub lords of the boy should be the ruling planets of the girl at the 
time of birth and similarly the 7th cusp sign, star and sub lords of the girl should be the rul- 
ing planets of the boy at birth. The occupant of the 7th in the respective charts can be taken 
as a ruling planet for this purpose. 


KPDP No. 8: Likelihood of marriage with this boy and girl 
The ruling planets of the boy at the time of birth should be the significators for 2.7.11 for 
the girl and vice-versa. 


KP Ezine December 2013 18 


KPDP No. 9: Smoothness in married life 

See whether the 11th cusp sub lords in the charts of the boy and the girl are in any way 
connected to houses 6,8,12 in any manner, in their respective charts. If they are not con- 
nected full marks can be given. Otherwise marks will have to be awarded proportionately. 


KPDP No. 10: Whether the period lords now operating in both charts indicate desirability 

of matching for marriage 

I. At the time of matching if either is running 'A' Dasa, 'B' Bukthi and 'C' Anthara, see 
whether A,B,C are the ruling planets at the time of birth of the other. 

II. The planets deposited in the star of the above A, B, C will be the ruling planets at the 
time of birth of the other. 

Either (i) or (ii) above should be there. Accordingly give marks proportionately. 


After totaling the marks obtained as above, divide the same by 1000 and arrive at the over- 
all percentage of matching. 


2. Anything above 50% score can be taken as matching. But for happy married life the 
overall matching percentage should cross 75% minimum. 


3. These KPDP marriage matching rules, framed by Shri Kuppu Ganapathi, can be utilized 
in many ways, for example, if one wants to know whether A and B can become partners in 
a business venture. It means getting a partner to do partnership business, the compatibil- 
ity chart i.e. KPDP will clearly throw light on it. Similarly if there is difference of opinion be- 
tween a boss and his subordinate or between the owner of a company and its top executive 
etc.

Aspects Uncovered by KPDP Matching Rules 


4. The KPDP marriage matching report covers the above mentioned ten marriage matching 
criteria of the horoscopes of a boy and a girl. However, this report does not cover other as- 
pects of marriage matching, such as longevity, education, health, child birth, career pro- 
spects and financial status. 


5. There is no practice of Mars Dosha in KP, although the traditional criteria of Mars Dosha 
are explained in details in KP Reader IV, pages 51-69. And it is concluded that not Mars 
alone, any planet can cause such undesirable effect of disagreement, dispute, divorce etc 
among the couple provided they happen to be deposited in such a position of the significa- 
tor of 6 or 10 or 12. (ibid page 69) 


6. In addition the traditional way of marriage matching for a native with Mars Dosha to 


marry with another one with Mars Dosha (KP Reader IV, page 68) is like adding more fire to 
a house which is already in fire. It does not agree with the KP principle to throw water and 


KP Ezine December 2013 19 


send when a house is in fire. (KP Reader VI, page 319) 
Useful Indication of KPDP No. 10 


7. The results of Kanak Bosmia’s study on 106 KPDP matching charts on 18 December 
2006 are as follows: 


Out of 29 marriage matching reports of “multi-marriage and divorce” cases, 25 matching 
reports (86.20%) with the KPDP criterion no. 10 score of “less than 50%” on the day of mar- 
riage had divorce. 


Out of 12 marriage matching reports of “single marriage and divorce” cases, 11 matching 
reports (91.67%) with the KPDP criterion no. 10 score of “less than 50%” on the day of mar- 
riage had divorce. 


Out of 65 matching reports of “single marriage” cases, 32 matching reports (49.23%) had 
the KPDP criterion no. 10 score of “50% and more “ on the day of marriage. 


8. In combination of the results of the above study on 106 KPDP matching reports and his 
extensive experience of KDPD marriage matching, Kanak Bosmia’s finding is that the KPDP 
criterion no. 10 (Whether the period lords operating at the time of matching in both charts 
indicate desirability for matching for marriage) score is more important than the overall 
matching score, and more than 50% score of the criterion no. 10 is preferable for marriage 
matching in order to prevent the possibility of separation or divorce. 


9. Whenever a misunderstanding or problem rises in married life, it is advisable to check 
how is the score of the KPDP criterion no. 10 at that time. As long as this score is “higher 
than 50%”, the problem may not be so serious that can be solved by mutual understanding. 
But this score is significantly “lower than 50%”, the problem may be serious for a possible 
separation or divorce.

7 Will i win this legal case filed against me? 
: a By: Gunti Nagaraju y 
M.com CAIIB, Retired Bank officer 
KP astrologer 
12-13-668/5/2, Second floor, Nagarjuna Nagar, 
Tarnaka,Secunderabad- 500 017; 
Tel: 040-27 172206; 9490752371 
Email: gunti.nagaraju@gmail.com 





The term litigation refers to the process of contesting in a court of law. It is a judicial contest 
to establish and enforce legal rights, a legal proceeding in a court. Litigation can be either 
criminal or civil proceedings. 


Commercial litigation is in general any type of legal controversy related to business issues. 
Cases that fall under this category include breaches of contract, employment disputes, dis- 
putes with business relationships, breach of fiduciary duty, debt collection commercial liti- 
gation etc. 


As we, all know that a controversy before a court or a "lawsuit" is commonly referred to as 
“litigation”. If litigation is one way that people and companies resolve disputes arising out of 
an infinite variety of factual circumstances. In the modern world these types of practices are 
on an increase, and due to the changes in the nature of the people they are more inclined 
towards taking things to court rather than solving them amicably. 


The incidence of litigation can be checked and the prospects of the outcome can be known 
by astrology. For this purpose K.P. system has laid out certain specific rules which are fur- 
nished hereunder. 


K.P. RULE AND COURT CASE 


Court case —- win or loss 

If the sub lord of 6 or 118 cusp signifies house 2,6,10,11, then one can win in court case 
during the joint period of significators of 6,11. Houses 5,8,12 indicate loss in court case and 
houses 3,9 show compromise. 


Appeal- Successful or not 

If the sub lord of the 3rd cusp is deposited in the constellation of a planet which is the sig- 
nificator of 6 and 11, one will have success. But if the sub lord of the 3rd cusp is deposited 
in the constellation of a planet who is the significator of houses 5 and 12, one cannot have 
success. (KP Reader VI, page 170) 


With the help of above K.P. rules on “winning any appeal, court case or litigation” I would 
like to discuss a case study of my friend Mr S.Y. whose birth details are furnished hereun- 
der. 


Mr. S.Y. was a bank employee and had some professional problems during his tenure of of- 
fice. As opined by the bank, he committed some mistakes while discharging his duties, and 
was accused and a court case was filed against him. It was contested by the native, and af- 
ter a prolonged legal battle, he won the court case.

Nature of Intercepted Signs 


By: Tin Win 
Email: tw853@yahoo.com 





What are intercepted signs ? 


Intercepted signs or blank signs are the zodiac signs where any house cusp does not fall. 
Intercepted signs always occur in opposing pairs, and more than one house cusps fall in 
some signs making some houses larger and consequently others smaller. 


When do they appear? 


The equal house system with all houses 30° degrees each makes intercepted signs impos- 
sible. They appear in the unequal house systems, such as Placidus, Koch, Campanus, Re- 
giomontanus, Topocentric etc. 


At the lower latitudes like India their appearance is rare but the higher latitude, the more 
likely are extremely large houses with more intercepted signs since the lines marking divi- 
sions of latitude become increasingly closer together, as shown in the charts attached. 


How do they appear? 


Ch- 1: Indian chart at 30n19, Placidus, 2™4 house is larger by 32° 39’ due to one of 2 inter- 
cepted signs, and 6 house is smaller by 23° 35’ because of 2 cusps falling in one sign. 


Ch- 2: Scotland chart at 51n38, Placidus, 1st house is very large by 42° 54’ due to one of 4 
intercepted signs, and 6th house is very small by 15° 49’ because of 2 cusps falling in one 
sign. 


Ch- 8: Finland chart at 60n10, Placidus, 1st house is extremely large by 77° 36' due to 2 
consecutive intercepted signs out of 4 intercepted signs, and 6‘ house is very small by 
13° 33' because of 2 cusps falling in one sign. 


Ch- 10: Polar region chart at 77n40, Topocentric, reverse order of houses, 2" house is 
very large by 49° O6' due to one of 4 intercepted signs, and 34 house is extremely small by 
9° 15’ because of 3 cusps falling in one sign. 


Ch- 21: Male, TOB 06:05 AM, Tarko-Sale, Russia, 64n55, Placidus: 1st house is extremely 
large by 96° 48’ due to one of two 3 consecutive intercepted signs, and 5 house is excep- 
tionally small by 6° 37' because of 4 cusps falling in one sign. In this chart 6 signs are in- 
tercepted and 4 cusps fall in 2 signs. 


At latitudes between 51 and 53 degrees north around Edmonton, Canada, where Chris 
McRae has lived most of her life, about 82 percent of all charts contain at least one set 
of intercepted signs, about 10 per cent have two sets in pne house and about 10 percent 
have no interceptions at all by using the Placidus house system. (Chris McRae, Under- 
standing Interception - A Key to Unlocking the Door, American Fedration of Astrologers, 
2000) 


Virtually everyone in the UK, which is located between 50 and 59 degrees north latitude, 
has at least one pair of interceptions. Many have two, especially the Scots to become the 


KP Ezine December 2013 47 


New Age leaders. India, by contrast, is barely north of the equator. Interceptions in that part 
of the world are extremely rare. This is why India is along with all its many holy men, sages, 
gurus and pandits. (Alice Millers, Interceptions Heralds of a New Age, American Federation 
of Astrologers, 2009) 


“A few months ago I reviewed a book by Alice Miller that claimed intercepted houses make 
the individual somehow “special”, unique and gifted, an idea I found silly. For one thing, the 
further north you go, the more signs get intercepted. In India interceptions are quite rare. In 
Scotland, it’s exactly the reverse.” (David R. Roell, Skeet Shooting for Astrologers, Astrology 
Classic, 2011, p 121)

guest at the grand finale.

winning), success is assured in the joint period (DBAS) of significators of 1, 6, 11. 

(Note: 6th is stronger than 11, 11th is stronger than 1.)

sub of Moon. Planet Saturn is the occupant of 3, owner of 6 and 7. Saturn having no planet 
in its stars is the CSL of houses 6, 10. Starlord Rahu is the occupant of 2. Rahu is con-

Hints 

If the cuspal sub lord of the 6th or 10th be the significator of 2, 6, 10 or 11 permanent sta- 
tus in service or earning is promised during the joint period of the significators of 2, 6, 10 
and 11. 


Cuspal sub lord 


Cusps 6‘ (Sagittarius 20°.02’.16”): 

The sub lord of 6 cusp is Rahu. Rahu is in the star of Saturn and sub of Jupiter. Rahu is 
in 5. Rahu is aspected by Mars. Mars is occupant of 2, owner of 5, 10. Star lord Saturn is 
occupant of 3, owner of 7, 8. Sub lord Jupiter is occupant of 9, owner of 6, 9. No planet in 
the star of Jupiter and Jupiter is CSL of 3, 12. Thus 6 cusp sub lord Rahu signifies 8 and 
is connected with 5, 2, 10, 6, 9. Hence permanent status in service is promised. 


Cusps 10+ (Aries 16°.50’.26”): 

The sub lord of 10t8 cusp is Moon. Moon is in the star of Venus and sub of Saturn. Moon is 
occupant of 6, owner of 1. Star lord Venus is in 9, owner of 4, 11. Sub lord Saturn is occu- 
pant of 3, owner of 7, 8. Thus 10% cusp sub lord Moon signifies 9, 4, 11 and is connected 
with 6, 1, 3, 7, 8. Hence permanent status in service is promised.

and dejection). This does not indicate continuity in the same job; hence you will not get per- 
manent status in the present job, but you will change the job.

given interview in a new company on 27th February, and he was selected in a permanent 
status. There are some necessary formalities he has to conduct on company’s behalf and he 
has to join the new company from 1st April 2013 onwards.

Question-Answer 


By: Tin Win 
Email: tw853@yahoo.com 





Question-1: Counting 6,8,12 houses from Lagna or Particular Sign 


In KP reader III 10% Edition 2005, pg-135 Para (b) 
Under Chapter “How to Judge whether a planet is a benefice or a Malefic “ 


Reads As 

(b) lord of the second house will prove to be benefic to the matter signified by 
he second house, if it dose not occupy the constellation and sub of the significator of the 
houses 6, 8, and 12 counted from lagna. Similarly , foreach house we have to note 
whether the significator of the house , is posited in the constellation and sub of the signifi- 
cator of the houses 6, 8, and 12 counted from that particular sign. If any planet is so pos- 
ited or if it is conjoined with the lords of such houses , the planet offers adverse results sig- 
nified by it by lordship. The above is general principle. 


Sir, in the above statement, it says for second house count from lagna 
And for other (EACH) houses Count from that house sign 
Which is correct? Please Help. 


Answer- Il: 


1. The 6, 8 and 12 houses are to be counted from the house under consideration, as origi- 
nally mentioned in “Krishnamurti Padhdhati, Vol. 2”, by Guru ji K.S.K., Sagar Publica- 
tions, 1966 , p 41, below: 


(B) Lord of the second house will prove to be a benefic to the 
matters signified by the second house, if it does not occupy the 
houses 6, 8 and 12 counted from the second house, or conjoined 
with the lords of houses 6, 8 and 12 counted from Lagna. Similarly, 
for each house we have to note whether the lord of the house is posited 
in the houses 6, 8 and 12 counted from that particular sign. Jf any 
planet is so posited or if itis conjoined with the lords of such 
houses, the planet becomes a malefic to offer adverse results 
signified by it by lordship, The above is the general principle. 

But according to Krishnamurti Padhdhati, the planet which is 

2. The above general principle is not always working. The KP fundamental rule is as given 
under (KP Reader III, p 135/ 1971 edition p 129; KP Reader V p 135/ 1971 edition p 129), 
i.e. just after the above mentioned general principle: 

“But according to Krishnamuriti system the planet which is considered to be a benefic by 


lordship offers the results signified by it, through the planet deposited in its constellation. 
Beneficial planets offer their results through the depositors in their constellation, only when 


KP Ezine December 2013 80 


the sub is also governed by a benefic. If the sub is ruled by a malefic the depositors cannot 
bring out favourable results. For example, to a Scorpio-born. Jupiter is the lord of 2 and 5. 
Jupiter is not only the chief governor for children but also by owning the houses 2 and 5 it 
signifies the birth of children to that person. Jupiter rules the stars Punarvasu, Visaka 

and Poorvapathrapada. If a planet occupy anyone of these stars then that planet has to 
offer the results indicated by Jupiter. If the sub is governed by lord of 11 then the person 
gets a child. But if the sub is ruled by lord of 12, no child will be born during the period 
of the planet in the sub governed by lord of 12. Therefore, a,planet occupying Punarvasu 
Nakshathra and Mercury sub will give a child. So one is to understand that the planet 
which either occupies a constellation or transits in a constellation, is the source by which 
one has his desire fulfilled. The lord of the constellation indicates the nature of the result, 
the sub shows whether it is desirable or undesirable. 

Hence Planet is the source, constellation indicates nature of the result and the SUB 
is a deciding factor whether the matter is favourable or not.” 


3. “In order to know what each planet can contribute always consider its sub lord”. (KP 
Reader III page 362/ 1971 edition, practical part p194) Generally if the sub lord occupies 
or owns houses 6, 8, 12 from a house occupied or owned by a planet or its star, the sub 
lord may not favor the house matters. However out of houses 6,8,12, only the 12th position 
to any house is clearly negative or detrimental for that house. For example, Female born 
on 4 November 1983, at 2:04 p.m., hr 5 west, in Brunswick, GA (US), 81w30, 31n09, KP 
New Ayanamsa 23° 32' 27”, the 5t cuspal sub lord is Jupiter. 


4. Jupiter is in 10, lord of 2,11, in the star of Mercury in 9, lord of 5,8 and sub of Venus in 
7, lord of 4,9. 


From house 10, houses 6,8,12 are houses 3,5,9, and the sub lord does not favor house 10 
matters as it signifies 9, which is negative 12 to 10. 

From house 2, houses 6,8,12 are houses 7,9,1 and generally the sub lord may not favor 
house 2 matters as it signifies 9, which is 8 from 2. 

From house 11, houses 6,8,12 are houses 4,6,10, and generally the sub lord may not favor 
house 11 matters as it signifies 4, which is 6% from 11. 

From house 9, houses 6,8,12 are houses 2,4,8, and generally the sub lord may not favor 
house 9 matters as it signifies 4, which is 8 from 9. In fact the sub lord favors house 9 
matters by signifying the same house 9. 

From house 5, houses 6,8,12 are houses 10,12,4, and the sub lord does not favor house 5 
matters as it signifies 4, which is negative 12‘ from 5. 

From house 8, houses 6,8,12 are houses 1,3,7, and the sub lord does not favor house 9 
matters as it signifies 7, which is negative 12‘ from 8. 


Jupiter as “Dasa lord” is not conducive to child birth as houses 2,5,11 are not favorable by 
the sub lord. But child birth is promised as long as 2,5,11 are signified by Jupiter as a 
“cuspal sub lord”.

Answer- 4: No aspects of Rahu/ Ketu 


1. The Western aspect “Jupiter square Rahu and Kethu” mentioned on page 324 of 
"Astrology for Beginners, Vol. 3'" by K. Subramaniam, for the horary chart, “Horary no. 
72, date and time of judgment 20-12-1974, 9:25 p.m. at Madras, 13° N 4 , 80° E 17’, 
means that “Jupiter casts square aspect on Rahu and Kethu;” but Rahu and Kethu 

do not cast square aspect on Jupiter, by looking for Jupiter row and Rahu/ Ketu rows 


in the following Western aspects print-out of KPAstro 4.1 for that horary chart.

2. There is no contradiction regarding that Nodes (Rahu/ Ketu) do not aspect any planet 
or any house because they are only the sensitive and powerful intersecting points in the 
pathway of Sun and Moon and they are not having any physical body which can 

be seen through a telescope as we can see all the other planets. This is the reason why 
they are called shadowy planets without having any own sign in the Zodiac. 


3. In the KP Readers, only Hindu aspects are practically and effectively applied in solving 
the examples, except some minor applications of Western aspects here and there. Moreo- 
ver the significator by aspect/ conjunction is the last resort of rank E weak significator 
after A to D rank significators. And only those planets aspected by A to D significators are 
to be taken into consideration as rank E significator. 

http: //groups.yahoo.com/neo/groups/k p system/conversations/topics/7295 


4. If all Hindu and Western aspects are taken into consideration, most planets can be the 
significator of almost all houses. Another problem is how to reconcile the “good and bad” 
or “favorable and adverse” Western aspects with the KP significators by occupation and 
lordship at the planet, star and sub levels. 


5. The idea of closer conjunction or aspect, its effect becoming stronger can be applied by 
using Hindu aspects with (Western practice of) orb. Such way is applied in the 4 step theo- 
ry with basic orb 3° N 20’. 


Different Views Regarding the Aspects of Rahu and Ketu 


6. The aspects of Rahu/Ketu are not mentioned or applied in the KP Readers. Considera- 
tion of the aspects of Rahu/Ketu are rarely found in the K.P. & Astrology Year Book, 
1996, p 72; 1999, p 26, and 2002, pp 82 & 84. 


7. Ernst Wilhelm has said in his “Vault of the Heavens: Treatise on Vedic Astrology”, Kala 
Occult Publishers, 2001, p 196 that there are different views regarding the aspects of Ra- 
hu and Ketu. Some do not consider them to have any aspect at all. Those who do consider 
Rahu and Ketu to have aspects, generally consider them to aspect the 5th, 7th and 9th 
with full strength, similar to Jupiter's aspect. However, none of the astrological treatises 
ascribed to any of the rishis gives aspects to Rahu and Ketu. He believes that due to a fac- 
tor called Argala, which exerts a type of influence on a planet, Rahu and Ketu have mis- 
takenly been thought to aspect the 5th and 9th places from them. Argala is not a com- 
monly used, nor a commonly understood factor in astrology. His belief is that Rahu and 
Ketu do exert an influence onto the 5 and 9th places from them, but through Argala, not 
through aspect. An aspect influences a planet directly due to the aspecting planet’s na- 
ture, its colors what it aspects accordingly. Rahu and Ketu influencing the 5th and 9th do 
not do this. I have found that trying to use planetary aspects for Rahu and Ketu will be 
misleading and a source of confusion when making predictions. Wendy Wasicek says that 
Maharishi Parashara is quite specific about the planets’ aspects but nowhere does he at- 
tributes any (specific) aspect to the nodes. 

http: //www.jyotishvidya.com/nodes.htm 


8. Dr. P. S. Sastri has said in his notes in “Uttara Kalamrita Kalidasa”, Ranjan Publica- 
tions, 2001, page 43 that according to Parasara, Rahu aspects 5, 7, 9, and 12 fully. James 
Braha has changed his view on nodal aspects in "The Art & Practice of Ancient Hindu As- 
trology", Hermetician Pr, 2001, p 388, by saying that after years of research he found that 
sage Parasara was correct and the aspects should be noticed, although most Indian astrol- 
ogers he has met do not use the aspects. 


9. Robert Koch’s compilation of the classical references to the aspects of Rahu and Ketu is: 


BPHS, Chapter 9, verses 7-11; 33, 36; 33, 50; Jataka Parijata: 3, 42; 4, 4; 4, 59; 6, 87; 6, 
97; 8, 50; 8, 51; 8, 52; Jaimini Sutram: 1, 7. It is not specified whether such aspects are 


KP Ezine December 2013 84 


on 5 and 9, or whether they are by Rashi drishti. Other references given by some are: BPHS 
(Khemraj-Shrikrishndas- edition) in chapter 47,verse 26, says: SUT-MADAN-NAV-ANTE 
POORN DRISHTIM TAMASYA YUGAL-DASHAM GEHE CH ARDH DRISHTIM VADANTI SA- 
HAJ-RIPU VIPASHYAN PAD DRISHTI, meaning Rahu and Ketu have full aspect on 5-7-9- 
12; Jatak-Parijat ch. 2 verse 32 says Rahu's aspect is downward, confirming Rahu has as- 
pect. But the references themselves do not agree upon the results. Even Varahamihira did 
not exclusively touch Rahu/ Ketu in his classic Brihat Jataka. Rahu's aspect has not been 
mentioned also in Kalyana Varmas Saravali.

Endometriosis Disease 


By: Tin Win 
Email: tw853@yahoo.com 








Endometriosis 
Endometriosis is a painful, chronic disease that occurs when cells from the lining of the 


womb (uterus) grow outside the uterus. The misplaced fragments of tissue develop and 
bleed in response to the hormones of the menstrual cycle. In turn, this causes inflammation 
and damage in nearby tissues. Symptoms of endometriosis include cyclic pelvic pain, exces- 
sive bleeding, and problems getting pregnant (infertility).

What is Leukemia? 


In pathology - blood consists of three types of cells and cell fragments floating in liquid 
called plasma. These cellular components are: 
1. Red Blood Cells ("erythrocytes," "RBCs") - oxygen-carrying cells 
2. White Blood Cells ("leukocytes," "WBCs") - cells that help make up the body's im- 
mune system 
3. Platelets ("thrombocytes") - fragments of cells that play an important role in for- 
mation of blood clots. 


The total number of white blood cells normally ranges from 4 million to 11 million cells per 
milliliter of blood. Leukemias are a group of diseases characterized by an abnormal in- 
creased numbers of white cells in the blood and bone marrow. 


In Astrology - White Blood Corpuscles- These are said to be destroyers of the body and to 
form a nucleus for mineral deposits. They are manufactured in the Spleen and are princi- 
pally the work of Saturn. During anger and also during diseases and various afflictions, 
they pass through the wall of the blood vessels and deposit themselves in weakened or dis- 
eased tissues and form a nucleus for the increased deposit of mineral wastes of the body, 
forming tumors, ulcers. (Encyclopaedia of Medical Astrology, by Dr. H. L. Cornell, M. D., D. 
A.)

Longevity analysis 

1st cuspal sub lord Venus+ is in house 11, owner of houses 3, 8. Having no planet in its 
stars, Venust+ is the CSL of houses 1, 2, 7, 8. This Venus+ is in the star of Sun in house 10, 
owner of house 6, and sub of Saturn+ in house 8, owner of houses 11, 12, signifying long 
life indicators of 1,11, against short life indicators of 2 (Maraka), 6 (sickness), 7 (Maraka & 
Badhaka), 8 (danger to life) and 12 (end of life). Hence the 1st CSL indicates short life, say 
up to 1 year and 3 months. 


For cross check, the chart is rotated to 10 cusp as Ascendant. Counting from 10 house, 
10% cuspal sub lord Rahu is in house 10, conj. Moon in house 11, owner of house 8 and 
Saturn+ in house 11, owner of houses 2, 3, aspected by Jupiter in house 7 (Badhaka, Mara- 
ka), owner of houses 1, 4; Rahu is in Libra sign of Venus+ in house 2, owner of houses 6, 
11, having no planet in its stars, Venus+ is the CSL of houses 4,5,10,11. This Rahu is in the 
star of own Rahu, and sub of Saturn+ in house 11, owner of houses 2, 3. The 10%» CSL Ra- 
hu signifies long life indicators of houses 1, 5, 11, against short life indicators of 2 (Maraka), 
6 (sickness), 7 (Maraka & Badhaka), 8 (danger to life) and 12 (end of life). Thus 10 CSL in- 
dicates short to medium life, say up to 2 and half years.

TSP IN NUT SHELL - 

A. If Sub Sub lord of the Asc Sub Sub lord tallies with —

Recovery of Lost Mobile 


By: Er. V.K Sharma, B.E. (Elect), 
JYOTISHVID (PRASHER), K.P HORARATNA 
Superintending Engineer (Retired.), 
Punjab State Electricity Board, 
Address: #104, City Enclave, Zirakpur, 
Mohali (Chandigarh). 





An electrician who was doing electric wiring at our residence seemed quite disturbed. I 
asked him the reason for the same. He told me that someone has stolen his personnel mo- 
bile from his shop and he sought my help to check astrologically whether the lost mobile 
will be found or not. I asked him to intimate any horary number between 1 and 249, after 
some thought he told horary number as 7. Accordingly I made the horary map for the said 
number immediately in his presence on dated 5-2-2008 at 1:15 P.M. at Chandigarh. 


Moon reveals the nature of query. 

Moon is in 10 and in the star of Sun in 11 lord of 6 and in the sub of Rahu in 11. Rahu is in 
the sign of Saturn lord of 11 and 12. Hence Moon is the significator of 12 [loss] and 11 [to 
regain]. Thus query relates to the loss of movable property [mobile] and its regaining. 


Recovery of lost property 

As per HORARY ASTROLOGY Sixth KP Reader page 235 written by sh K.S.Krishnamurti, if 
the significators of the houses 2, 6 and 11 agree [counted from the house indicating the per- 
son whose property is lost] with the ruling planets of the day, the property lost will be Re- 
covered. If the ruling planets are connected with 5, 8 and 12 houses it is lost once for all.

ASC VENUS MOON MERC 
MOON SATURN SUN RAHU 
DAY LORD MARS 


WHO IS THE THIEF? 

7h sublord indicates thief. Here 7 sublord is Rahu in 11. As Rahu is in Aquarius a mesca- 
line sign, thief will be male, and as Rahu is significator of 11, thief will be known person or 
friend. 


CHECK SIGNIFICATORS OF RULING PLANETS 


VENUS is in 9 lord of 2 and 7 and it is in the star of Venus in 9 lord of 2 and 7, in the sub 
of Jupiter in 9 lord of 10. Hence Venus is the significator of 2 and 10. 


MOON is in 11, in the star of sun in 11 lord of 6, and in the sub of Rahu in 11. Hence 
Moon is the significator of 6 and 11. 


MARS is in 2, again in the star of Mars in 3, and in the sub of Mercury in 11 lord of 3 and 
4. No planet is in the star of Mercury and Mercury is the CSL of 6,12. So Mars is the sig- 
nificator of 6 and 11. 


SUN is in 11 lord of 6, in the star of Moon in 10, and in the sub of Venus in 9 lord of 2. 
Hence Sun is the significator of 2 and 6. 


SATURAN is lord of 11 and it is in the star of Ketu, in sign of Sun lord of 6, and Sat is in the 
sub of Mercury in 11. No planet is in the star of Mercury, and Mercury is the CSL of 6,12. 
Hence SATURAN signifies 6 and 11.

Proposal for ‘Six Fold Significator Table’ 


Based on the above three examples, in July 2008 in the K-P-system discussion Yahoo 
group, R. Dhanabalan had proposed to convert the existing “four” fold significator table 
(grade A, B, C, D) in the six KP Readers into the “six fold significator table” with “sub” as be- 
low: 

Six Fold Significators — Planet View 


Planets Occupants |Planets' /Planets

Sub of Star of 
House Lord

* House 1 to 12 column for “Six Fold Significators — House View” 
Note: Column A & D are added for the “sub” to the usual grade A, B, C, D (here B, C, 
E, F) significators. 


Why ‘six fold significator table’ is not acceptable? 
This idea of the “six fold significator table” had been discussed unacceptable because of the 
following reasons: 


1. With compared to only 3 examples with “sub”, the usual “four” fold significators (grade 
A, B, C, D) without “sub" like in the six KP Readers have been used in 13 examples on pp 
97, 74, 118, 139, 236, 244, 256, 269, 276-277, 301, 303, 308 and 333 of “Krishnamurti 
Padhdhati, Vol. 2, Sagar Publications, 1966”; 
Out of these 3 examples with :sub”, only the first example chart, at 10 p.m. on 9-3-1923, on 
p 110 under “Free from Debts" have been reprinted in the KP Reader III, 1971 edition, prac- 
tical part, p 59 (new edition p 216 ) under “Free from Debts", but “without” the following 
paragraph with “sub”: 
"According to Krishnamurty Paddhathi, one can borrow money during the dasas and bhutkties 
of: 

planets in the star or “sub” of occupants of 6th house; 

occupants of 6th house; 

planets in the star or "sub” of lord of 6th house; 

the lord of 6th house; 

planets conjoined with or aspected by any of these planets.” 
(Krishnamurti Padhdhati, Vol. 2, Sagar Publications, 1966, p 113) 
3. Other two examples regarding second chart, at 6-02 p.m. on 3-11-1839 under “Child 
Birth — When”, on p 272, and third chart, at 11-25 a.m. on 24-9-1965 under “Time of 
Transfer” on p 318 (Krishnamurti Padhdhati, Vol. 2, Sagar Publications, 1966) are no more 
included in any of the six KP Readers at all. 
Needles to say, only the usual four fold (grade A, B, C, D) significators have been found 
consistently applied in the KP Reader II], pp 342; KP Reader IV, pp 118, 128, 201; KP 
Reader V pp 149, 201; KP Reader VI pp 157, 197, 247 etc., KP SWs and the KP literature in 
general. 


Why the “six fold significator table” is not used in the six KP Readers? 


KP Ezine lanuarv 2014 47 


The main reason of not using the “six fold significator table” in the six KP readers in partic- 
ular and KP practice in general is that using the sub’s_ signication as significator will 
contradict with the following KP fundamental principle of sub as a decider in choosing the 
fruitful significators: 


"Planet is the source, constellation indicates nature of the results, and the SUB is deciding 
factor whether the matter is favourable or not." (Krishnamurti Padhdhati, Volume 2, Sugar 
Publication, Jan 1966, p 41; KP Reader III, V, VI) "This discovery has crowned me with suc- 
cess.” (KP Reader III , pp 1386-137/ 197 ledition, theory part pp 129-130, KP Reader V, pp 
136-137/ 1971 edition 129-130 & KP Reader VI, pp 41, pp 81-82) 


When majority of planets are connected with the houses 2, 7 and 11, select the useful ones 
which agree with ruling planets at the time of judgment. If a planet is in such a position that 
its sub lord is connected with the houses 2, 7 and 11, then this planet is useful. But if the sub 
is lord of 1, 6, 10 and is the significator of 12 house, marriage cannot take place. (KP Reader 
IV, p 118) 


In choosing fruitful significators for marriage, reject those planets which are in the sub of 
planets in 1, 6 and 10, as these are the 12% houses to the houses 2, 7 and 11, and select the 
planets that are on the sub of the planets signifying 2, 7 and 11. (KP Reader IV, p 150) To se- 
lect the strongest significators, reject the planets that are not in the sub of lords of 2, 5 and 11. 
(ibid p 235) 


Whenever the significators are more in number the best method to select the beneficial ones 
and eliminate the tempters is to find out the ruling planets at the time of judgment and see 
which of them are common with the significators. (KP Reader VI, p 274, 276, 288-289) 


In this context of the sub lord being a decider but not a significator, K.M. Subramaniam 
stated at the beginning of his last 'Sublord Speaks' article LX of “K.P. & Astrology Year 
Book 1998” p 69, reprinted in “SUBLORD SPEAKS” - part 3, p 141, as below: 

Whether it is a planet or CUSPAL SUBLORD these are controlled by the cuspal sub lord and its 
signification only. 

As regards to a planet, the matter is seen through the star lord of that planet and the SUB 
LORD of that planet decides the result & how the matter is altered & enjoyed and suffered by 
the native. While we take the sub lord of the CUSP (all know the SUB LORD is a planet), we 
must be more careful, while dealing the subject. 

As told above, the CUSPAL SUB LORD is a PLANET. Here we must finalise the efficiency of the 
CUSPAL SUBLORD, by finding out the signification of the CUSPAL SUB LORD and any period 
runs under that planet signifying that house (CUSP), effects to get altered in those terms. To 
make it more clear for the students of KP, I like to discuss the following birth chart, as an ex- 


It is also followed by Chandrakant R. Bhatt as given under: 

The sub lord of the significator is the deciding factor regarding the matters of star lord. If the 
sub lord is harmonious to the matters indicated by the star lord, the significator gives favora- 
ble results. If the sub lord is detrimental to the matters indicated by the star lord, the significa- 
tor gives unfavorable results. (Nakshatra Chintamani, p 23-24) 


Observation 
Although the sub's signification cannot be considered as a ‘straight’ significator, the signifi- 
cation of a planet needs to be considered by houses of occupation and ownership at all 


three levels of the planet itself, its star and sub. And sub has a Say in assessing the matter 
even if the star lord does not indicate such matter.

If the 7 cuspal sub lord signifies houses 2,7,8,11 and is connected to Rahu or Saturn, 
marriage to a widow/widower is indicated during the joint dasa period (DBAS) of signifi- 
cators of houses 2,7,8,11. 


Question - 2: Promise of the Event 


We take the cuspal sub lord to see whether the event is promised or not to the native. 
Here, we see the three step signification of sub lord- i.e.(1) sub lord, (2) its star lord and 
(3) its sub lord position. The signification is arrived at its star lord i.e. (2) and its con- 
nection to the house is arrived from (1) and (38). 


In the examples narrated in KP readers - it is seen that Guruji has taken exclusively 
star lord signification and not the connectivity. For eg in Reader VI - Horary Astrology, 
page 192 (Any child for me? Who is sterile?) while analysing the chart he has taken only 
the signification at star level and declared sterile. 5th house sub lord Jupiter signifying 
1,4,8,9 and not connected to the required houses. So the person is sterile. But if we 
take the significations at three step the 5th CSL is Jupiter in Sun Star and Venus Sub- 
and the signification will be Jupiter in 9(1-4), Star lord Sun in 8(9), sub lord Venus in 6 
(6-11). So Jupiter signify 1,4,8,9 and connected with 6,11. Here 11th signification 
comes. There are many other examples quoted like this. I find it confused to arrive at 
especially when the negative is to be predicted. Sir, I am not questioning the Guruji's 
analysis and his greatest knowledge. 


Sir, I am a naive to the KP system. I shall be much obliged if you will kindly guide me 
on such matters. 


Answer- 2: 


You've raised a very relevant question in learning KP. It’s correct to see the three step 
signification of a planet (as cuspal sub lord or dasa period lord), its star and up to its 
sub level. Without considering the sub, it is not KP because KP is the sub lord theory 
only, nothing else. 


As you're aware, the KP significator table of grade A, B, C, D significators in the KP 
Readers as well as SW print-outs are up to the two step planet and star level only, and 
so it needs to see further up to the third level of sub. 


You're right that it’s confusing to conclude whether an event is promised or not. The 
general rule is that an event is promised as long as the cuspal sub lord concerned signi- 


KP Ezine lanuarv 2014 





49 


fies any of the required houses, for instance 2,7,11 for marriage, at any level of planet, its 
star and its sub. Negative houses to marriage 1,6,10,12 are for consideration of separation 
or divorce after marriage. 

But in the case of dasa period lord, both the positive and negative houses are to be consid- 
ered simultaneously in consideration of end result whether a dasa period lord, Dasa lord or 
Bhukti lord, is capable to give the positive result.

Should I take results of “ Sun in 10 or lord of 10” only or SUN’s satr-lord’s re- 
sult or take both results for that planet’s transiting period. 

Please clarify. Thank you Sir. 


Answer-3: 


All the results indicated by the constellation Sun as occupant of 10ts house and owner of 
2nd house will be experienced during the period of the planet situated in that (Sun) constel- 
lation. (KP Reader V: Transit, end of page 116) Occupant (10% signification) is stronger that 
owner (2"4 signification). 

As a general rule for a planet in transit, the results of ‘star and also sub’ in which that 
planet is transiting are to be considered by occupation and ownership as above. So it is to 
see in which star and sub a planet is transiting to consider the transit results of that plan- 
et. 


Question- 4: Time Zone Problem 


In the given chart details “Male, 04-09-1913, 21:30 pm, h 1 east of GMT, 44n10, 08e20, Sid 
time 19:56:44, KPNA 22:33:43, Asc. Ar 27:04:48”, the time zone is given as 1 hour, which 
according to worldtimezone.com is correct. However these are places (Italy) where DST is 
also followed. How do we make sure that DST is not applicable in this case? 


Answer- 4: 

It is a good question regarding the Time Zone of chart details. Here “hr 1 east” is the time 
difference to enter into the “Time Zone” of any astrological SW. This “time difference” is 
used in the AstroDatabank chart details provided by www.astro.com . In this time differ- 
ence the daylight savings time (if it’s applicable) is already adjusted, i.e. hr 1 east = TZ + 


KP Ezine lanuarv 2014 50 


DST. For example, in the following chart, time: 07:26 (= 07:26 AM ), 
Timezone EDT h4w (is daylight saving time) 


(h4w= TZ5 hr minus DST 1 hr) 

http: //www.astro.com/astro-databank/Bush, George W. 

In the original AstroDatabank 4.0 data SW, 
Time: EDT 07:26 EDT (+5:00) 

(DT indicates DST) 

If the DST is to be adjusted in the given TZ, it should be mentioned about DST. If not men- 
tioned about DST, it is assumed no need to adjust the given TZ with DST. 

To make sure whether DST is to be adjusted, calculate the chart as per given chart details 
and check whether given Sid. Time or Asc. position are more or less the same. For exam- 
ple, for the given chart, after entering “04-09-1913, 21:30 pm, h 1 east of GMT, 44n10, 
O8e20” into the following - - 


free “Astraura” SW: 

http: //www.astraura.org/Charter2/CharterVak3.aspx , 

it gives the same Sid. Time and a little different Asc. position due a small difference in the 
ayanamsa used, as shown under: 


Sid. Time: 19° 56' 44" 


27° Ar 5' 8.1828"- - Krittika - - Mar-Sun-Sun-Sat 





Krishnamurthy Ayanamsa: 22° 33' 08" (KP old ayanamsa) 
(KP new ayanamsa is 22° 33' 43") 


This Time Zone can also be checked by the history of application of DST, as shown in the 
link below: 


http: //www.timeanddate.com/worldclock/timezone.html?n=2 1 5&svear= 1900 





For the year 1913 of the given chart, the DST was found not applied. 
By using the ACS atlas supported SW like KPAstro, such TZ or DST problem does not rise, 
because the SW is automatically adjusting itself by showing whether DST is applied or 


not.

With Presidential Elections set for Feb. 2, Costa Rica 

Distrust of the two-party system, apathy, staggering public debt and rising prices appear to 
be moving more Costa Ricans to the left. 

By Jay Brodell (Bio and Archives) Monday, January 6, 2014 

Presidential elections are Feb. 2, and the candidate some label a Communist is running neck- 
and-neck with the establishment choice. 

Polls show that José Maria Villalta Florez-Estrada , a 36-year-old lawyer and candidate of the 
Partido Frente Amplio, may end up in a runoff. His party is the latest manifestation of the 
Communists in Costa Rica, and opponents are making much of this connection. 

There are 13 presidential candidates, but early polls showed that Johnny Araya Monge, the 
former long-time mayor of the capital, San José, would win in a walk. The 56-year-old Araya 
even avoided early campaign events, and most professional politicians and many in the public 
figured he was the next person to occupy Casa Presidencial. 

Villalta, a sitting member of the country’s unicameral legislature, came on strong with a lot of 
help from leftist students at the University de Costa Rica from where he was graduated and 
hosted an environmental show for years.. 

His ascent in the polls reflects the discontent with the economic situation, an ineffective cur- 
rent president, corruption and the two major parties that have run the nation for 50 years, 
Araya, the candidate of the center left Partido Liberaci6n Nacional, is the nephew of Luis Al- 
berto Monge, who was president in the mid-1980Os. He is the brother of the party’s unsuccess- 
ful 1992 presidential candidate. 

The fortunes of Liberacién have suffered under the current presidency of Laura Chinchilla Mi- 
randa, who decreed higher taxes and has been beset by multiple cases of corruption and bad 
judgment. 

Araya got an early boost when a popular physician and his apparent biggest opponent from 
the Partido Unidad Social Cristiana quit. 

Whether it is true or not, Araya is haunted by clouds of suspicion to the extent that he is 
called in the street 10 percent Johnny. 

Villalta is an opponent of and wants to renegotiate the free trade treaty with the United State. 
That agreement barely survived a referendum in 2007. He is a populist who supports state 
ownership, higher taxes on the wealthy and price controls. He opposes privatization of re- 
sources, concessions of government facilities such as highways and economic inequality. 
Recent television commercials from opponents link him to Communist Cuba and the current 
leadership in Venezuela and warn the public against giving him a vote. Some go so far as to 
label him a violent Communist due to his participation in some repeated confrontations and 
protests along with students at the legislature and in the streets. 

Polls also suggest that about a third of the electorate will not go to the polls for various reason. 
The country’s public debt has been estimated at more than 4 percent of gross domestic prod- 
uct. Tax evasion is widespread even as the central government institutes new levies. Institu- 
tions, such as the Caja Costarricense de Seguro Social, have had financial problems. This is 
the institution that provides nearly universal health care. The national budget is balanced 
nearly 50 percent with borrowed money. 

The country also has widespread immigration from nearby Nicaragua, much of it illegal.

Violent crime is rampant, and the country is a highway for drugs going north. 

Public employment has spiked as the central government tries to insulate itself from the world 
economic situation. 

Consequently there are enough problems to challenge any politician. 

Villalta offers a change vague enough that each voter can define it personally. The campaign 
seems to be well-funded and slick with attention to social media as well as traditional plat- 
forms. 

Liberaci6n National is the party of José Figueres Ferrer, the father of modern Costa Rica and 
the winner in the 1948 revolution who established the country’s broad social welfare policies. 
The party has a nationwide political network, something Frente Amplio does not. José Maria 
Figueres Olsen, the son of José and a former president himself, has begun campaigning 
strongly for Araya. 

The party also is that of two-time president Oscar Arias Sanchez, the Nobel Peace Prize laure- 
ate, who has not given his support. 

Villalta’s success in the polls generated deep concern in the commercial establishment. They 
fear a strongly socialist leader will bring more taxes and controls as well as chase away the 
lucrative North American tourist trade. 

Even if Villalta does not win, his popularity and presence on the ballot is likely to bring many 
of his party members into the legislature.

Background Note: Nach Baliye ('Nach' means Dance and 'Baliye' means partner or mate) is 
a dance, reality-television series on the Indian STAR Plus channel. The contestants are cou- 
ples (called 'jodis' in Hindi) who are television stars. The sixth season of the Indian televi- 
sion dance reality show Nach Baliye was premiered on November 9, 2013 on Star 
Plus channel. The series is broadcast on Star Plus, Saturday and Sunday evenings. Karan 
Wahi and Gautam Rode are the hosts for the sixth season. The judges are Sajid Khan, cho- 
reographer Terrence Lewis, and model-actress Shilpa Shetty. 

At the time of judgment, total five celebrity couples secured their place in the semi-final 
round of Nach Baliye Season 6. Their names are (1) Gurmeet Choudhary & Debina Bonner- 
jee, (2) Ripu Daman Handa & Shivangi Verma, (3) Rithvik Dhanjani & Asha Negi, (4) Vinod 
Thakur & Raksha Thakur; and (5) Kiku Sharda & Priyanka Sharda. One couple will be 
eliminated in semi-final round on 25th January 2014 and the Grand Finale with final four 
couples will be held on coming Saturday & Sunday i.e. on 1st & 2d February 2014. The 
winner of the title will be announced on 2™4 February 2014. 


Hints: 

If 6 or 11 cuspal sublord signifies 6 (defeat to opponent, being 12‘ from 7 loss of oppo- 
nent), 11 (reputation as a winner, fulfillment of desire, success), 1 (self-efforts for winning), 
success is assured in the joint period (DBAS) of significators of 1, 6, 11. (Note: 6 is strong- 
er than 11, 11 is stronger than 1) 


(Note: To win any sort of competition, 6, 11 houses are judged primarily, while 1 (Self- 
efforts for winning), 3 (one’s ability) and 10 (position) should be considered as supportive 
houses)

A Tribute to Suchitra Sen 


By: Tin Win 
Email: tw853@yahoo.com 








Ms. Sen had carved a special niche in the hearts of millions of Indians through her graceful 
cinematic presence. She was one of the first Indian artistes to win an international award 

at Moscow in 1963. Ms Sen’s versatility and range of performances, in a career spanning 
nearly three decades, mark a unique contribution to Indian cinema, and to Bengali 

films in particular’. 

- Prime Minister of India Manmohan Singh 


Suchitra Sen - beauty, talent, enigmatic - she adorned film world of Bengal with exquisite per- 
formances, graced Hindi films too! 
- Amitabh Bachchan 


1. The diva of Bengali cinema, Suchitra Sen, was born on 07/Apr/1931, 02:30 am LMT, TZ 
5:57 East of GMT, at Pabna, now in Bangladesh, 24 N OO, 89 E15; KP New Ayanamsa: 22° 
48' 26", Asc. Cp 18:21:35, Star: Jyeshta, Pada 1, Bal. Dasa: Mercury 16 Y, 1 M, 13 D, by 
KPAstro 4.1.

(success, fulfillment of desire);

es having no planet in its star; 

3. The 10th CSL Mars’ signification of houses 5,6,10 and 11, and connection to Venus (chief 
governor for music and melodious voice, movies) by sub lordship; 

4. Her elevated Mars (desire for action and physical energy) and Jupiter (expansion) in 5th 
house aspecting on 2™4 cusp (voice) and Venus (music, movies) in Aquarius (music, mov- 
ies), and this Venus opposing Neptune (music, movies) in 7th house (public relation- 
ships) and 5th sign Leo (music, movies, star-studded sign).

cient position of wealth. With her eloquent eyes and arresting voice Suchitra Sen was her 
own star; she worked on her terms, doing it better than most of her contemporaries. 





4. She married Dibanath Sen, son of wealthy Bengali industrialist Adinath Sen, in 1947 be- 
fore launching a successful acting career. There were rumors that the marriage suffered due 
to her successful acting career. She married during Ketu Dasa- Ketu Bhukti of significators 
of marriage houses 2,7,11. The signification of detrimental houses 1,6,10 to marriage and 
12 (loss) indicates the marriage to be suffered. 


5. For all her professional success, her marital life was on the rocks, but the consummate 
actress weaved her experiences into some of the roles she essayed. She was shooting for 
“Saat Pakey Badha”, co-starring Soumitra Chatterjee in 1963, when her married life was go- 
ing through its worst phase. But, she gave her best in this film and went on to win the best 
actress award for her role at the Moscow International Film Festival, July 7-21, 1963. She 
was the first Indian actress to win an international award. It was during her Venus- Rahu- 
Venus- Venus DBAS. Dasa- Antra- Sookshma lord Venus signifies the beneficial houses 
1,2,3,6,11, and 5 to win the award, 3,9,12 to travel to Moscow, and 1,4,6,8,12 for worst 
phase in married life. Bhukti lord Rahu signifies the beneficial houses 2,3,6,11, and 5 to 
win the award, 3,12 to travel to Moscow, and 4,6,8,12 for worst phase in married life.

2013 to 25th May 2013. So roughly I have predicted that his son will get married during 
the month of May 2013.

Father of a newly born child was very much worried about the health of his child who was 
under continuous treatment in P G I Chandigarh. He approached me on 6-11-2013 to 
check astrologically from the horoscope if there is any danger to her longevity, the details 
of his child are as under. 


Date of birth: 26-10-2013; Time of birth: 4 PM; Place of birth: Chandigarh 


Analysis 

If the cuspal sublord of the Asc be the significator of the Badhaka and Maraka houses, 
there is danger to the life during the joint period of the significators of the Badhaka and 
Maraka houses. 


If these significators be the cuspal joint rulers of the Asc or the 8th cusp their joint period 
is very critical. 


Further if Asc is in movable sign 11th house is the Badhaksthana, if Asc falls in a fixed 
sign 9th house is the Badhaksthana , if the Asc falls in a common sign the 7th house is 
the Badhaksthana. 


In the horoscope under reference Asc falls in common sign so 7th house is the 
Badhaksthana. 


Ascendant sublord 

In the horoscope under reference Asc sublord is Saturn in 8 lord of 12 and Saturn aspects 
house 2, and as Saturn is not having any planet in its stars it becomes strong significator 
of house 7 being sublord of 7th cusp. Further Saturn is in the star of Rahu in 8 and it is 
in the sub of Moon lord of 6. 


Hence Asc sublord signifies 2 [Maraka], 7[Maraka and Badhaka], 6[Sickness], 8[Danger to 
life], 12[Hospitalization]. So in view of the above Asc sublord denotes hospitalization and 
danger to survival of child or short life. 


8th cuspal sublori is Mercury in 8 lord of 4 and 7; it is in the star of Jupiter in 4 lord of 1 
and 10. It is in sub of Saturn in 8 lord of 12. Saturn aspects house 2 and 6. As Saturn is 
not having any planet in its star it becomes the strong significator of house 7 by being 
sublord of 7th cusp. Hence 8th cusp sublord signifies 2 [Maraka], 7 [Badhaka], 6 
[Sickness], 8 [Danger to life], 12[Hospital], 4 [End of life]. As 8th cusp sublord is connected 
with Maraka and Badhaka houses, it becomes evil for longevity of child. 


WHAT ABOUT AILMENT? 

6t cusp sublord is Jupiter in 4 lord of 1 and 10. It is again in the star of Jupiter in 4 lord 
of 1 and 10. It is in sub of Ketu in 2; Ketu is in the sign of Mars in 6 lord of 2 and 9, and is 
aspected by Saturn in 8 lord of 12 and Ketu is also aspected by Sun in 7. 6th cusp has 
linkage with Jupiter [liver, jaundice, enlargement of organs], Mars [sudden and painful 
disease], Saturn [lingering disease] and Sun [heart, blood, brain]. Also 6th cusp sublord 
signifies 2[Maraka] and 7[Badhaka], 8[Danger to life] 12[Confinement to bed / 
hospitalization]. (Horoscopes and Diseases by Sh Chandrakant R. Bhatt, pages 2-4)

KP - Marriage by love and inter cast 
By: Gunti Nagaraju 
M.com CAIIB, Retired Bank officer 
KP astrologer 
12-13-668/5/2, Second floor, Nagarjuna Nagar, 
Tarnaka,Secunderabad- 500 017; 
Tel: 040-27172206; 9490752371 


Email: gunti.nagaraju@gmail.com 





In every body’s life marriage plays an important role in deciding the course of life. Mar- 
riage is such an interesting subject that it makes everyone to be inquisitive to know about 
it even before it actually takes place in one’s life. The seventh house in every horoscope is 
the complement of the first, and represents the unifying of all that is separated or isolated 
in the ascendant. It signifies the transmutation of the passions into the pure love, the ex- 
change of intellect for wisdom and the perfect individualization of the conscious self. In 
view of the importance it has gained and attached it needs to be addressed very carefully 
while studying the chart of an individual. Marriage has different shades such as conven- 
tional marriage, love marriage, inter cast marriage, marriage by contract, just living to- 
gether as man and woman etc. and the subject is very exhaustive. In the present article I 
would like restrict myself to discuss about marriage, love marriage and inter cast marriage 
only with the aid of K.P system and its rules. 


Marriage promised or not— 

A) The VII cusp sub lord will guide and give the clue. For marriage, we have to see 2, 7, 11 
houses. 24 house denotes family and by marriage a new member will be added to the fam- 
ily. 74 house denotes marriage bondage. 11th house denotes permanent friendship be- 
tween the couple. 

If the VII cusp sub lord happens to be in a star of a planet, who is the significator of 2 or 7 
or 11, then only marriage is promised. 

Marriage will take place during the conjoined period of the significators of 2, 7 and 11 
houses in their Dasa, Bhukthi , Anthara and Sookshma periods. 


Love marriage- K.P. rule for materialization of love affair into marriage- 

K.P. rules say — 

(A) If 5th cusp sub lord is a strong significator of 7 and 11, love affair will materialize into 
marriage. 


(B) If 5th and 7th cusps are interconnected then the chances of materialization of love af- 
fair is confirmed provided they signify 5, 7 and 11 houses. 


(C) If the 5th cusp sub lord is in any way connected to 06 and 12 along with the significa- 
tions of 2, 5, 7 and 11—then the love affair will be a failure. 


(D) If 7th cusp sub lord is in any way connected to 5th along with 7—- one may marry a 
boy/girl loved by her/him. 


(E) If the 7th cusp sub lord is the significator of 5 and 11 which denotes love marriage and 
if it is connected with Rahu or Ketu, it indicates an inter cast marriage or /and unconven- 
tional marriage. 


(F) If 5 cusp sub lord signifies 6 — native’s lover will withdraw from love affair. 

(G) If 5t cusp sub lord signifies 12th —- native himself will drop the idea of love marriage. 

(H) To know whether the love affair is two-way or one sided — see 11 cusp (as it is the 5th 
cusp to opposite sex) and then judge.

Question- 1: Selection of Fruitful Significators 


I am writing this to seek your advise in understanding a problem which I encountered in 
your Article " KP for Beginners - Part 7 " published in KP Ezine Oct 2008 issue ( It is at- 
tached for your easy reference ). 

I refer to the Example Chart given on page No 6. 

My problems are regarding the selection of fruitful significators for marriage (Page No 8 ). 


Problem No. 1 


In this case, Moon is retained as a Fruitful Significator. But Moon is in the sub of 
Rahu which signifie house 11 as a Grade B significator and House 1 as a Grade A 
significator. It means that Moon signifies both successful house (11 ) and negating 
house (1 ).I think Moon is retained as there are no planets in Moon's Star. Am I cor- 
rect Sir ? 


Problem No. 2 


In this case we have selected 4 fruitful significators just by applying the rule ex- 
plained in point 7. (1). 


Now, Sir, Let us say we ended up in more than 4 significators (say 7 or 8 ) after 
applying the above Rule. What are the other Rules which should be followed for 
further elimination (in the order of priority)? 


I will be grateful if you kindly assist me in understanding the above problems. 


Answer- 1: 

Problem No. 1 

Based on the significator table of the attached example chart, Moon is taken as the signifi- 
cator of house 11 by Moon’s star lord Venus’ ownership of house 11. Moon’s sub lord Ra- 
hu is in house 11, in sign Taurus of Venus, owner of house 11. Moon is chosen as a fruit- 
ful significator by the following method in 7. (1): 


“7. In selecting the fruitful significators, 

1) select the planets, only if both the significator and its sub lord signify the 2,7 and 11 
houses, and reject those planets in the sub signifying only 1,6 and 10 as they are 12th 
house to the house 2,7 and 11;” 


Of course, as there are no planets in Moon's Star, Moon is the strong significator of 
houses 4,7 by being the sub lord of these houses, and here 7‘ strong signification is also 
another reason to select Moon as a fruitful significato for marriage. 


Problem No. 2 


Here are selection methods of fruitful significators in priority, depending on one's prefer- 
ence of the ruling planets: 


KP Ezine Februarv 2014 58 





1) Significators of planets with no planets in their stars, which are the strongest signifi- 
cators of houses under consideration by sub lordship to them, (Ref: KP Reader III p 
309, KPA 1991 July p 1 & November p 8), (Same as in the Golden Rule: to take the 
planets which are posited in the sub of significators whose constellations are not ten- 
anted. Ref: Astrosecrets & KP, Part II, 2003, pp 194-199); 

2) 2) Significators whose sub lords are the significators of houses under consideration; 
3) Significators which are the cuspal sub lords of houses under consideration; 

4) Significtors which are common with the Ruling Planets at the time of judgment; 

5) Significators appearing many times amongst the significators.

KP Ezine Februarv 2014 59 


Answer- 2: 


Sub’s Star 

1) Regardless of the planet’s sub lord being tenanted or untenanted, for the signification of 
a planet, the planet, its star lord and its sub lord should be considered by occupation and 
ownership, according to the following KP fundamental rule: 


"The planet is the source, constellation indicates nature of the result and the sub is a de- 
ciding factor whether the matter is favorable or not." 


KP goes with rationale, and it is the sub lord theory only. So it stops at the sub level. 


One should restrict up to the sub lord (3'4 step) of the planet. If the sub’s star lord (4 step) 
is further considered, it increases the double probability of the result. So it is not a correct 
approach. (Sharad C. Joshi: Nakshatra Chintan, KP-based, Part I p 36) 


4 Step Method 

2) The 2-step up to star lord is the stellar method; 3-step up to sub lord is KP method, and 
4-step up to the sub’s star is 4 step method, which is explained in “A Study Article on 4 
Step Theory in the KP-Ezine December 2007 issue”. The “Differences between KP and 4 
Step Method” are answered in the Question 8 of Q & A section, KP-Ezine October 2013 is- 
sue. There is an article of marriage prediction by 4 step method in this month KP-Ezine. 


Aspect/ Conj. 

3) In KP aspect/ conjunction is the grade E very weak signifcator to be used as the last re- 
sort only, and only the planet aspect/ conj. by the grade A,B,C,D significators are to be 
considered. (KP Reader IV pp 118, 128, 201; KP Reader VI pp 157, 197, 247) 


It is applicable at all three levels of planet, its star and sub but mainly in checking the con- 
nection to the karaka planets other than looking for signification.

Book Review- 
Nakshatra Chintan, KP-based, Part | & II 
By: Tin Win 
Email: tw853@yahoo.com 





Nakshatra Chintan, KP-based, Part I & II, 

by Sharad C. Joshi, 

Jyotish Bharati, 2001 

http: shop.saptarishisastrolo ~-com/index.php? 


page=details&prod=1911&cat=74&group=63 


Sharad ©. Joshi 





BEE eee 
oe ee ae 


we “I 
ewe eh 





This is a continued serial review of some of over one hundred KP based books in English. 
The present book “Nakshatra Chintan” is the third book of Sharad C. Joshi after review of 
his two books, namely: “Krishnamurti Padhadhati = Nirayan + Sayan” in the KP-Ezine April 
2013 issue and “Nakshatra Light” in the KP-Ezine August 2013 issue. 


In this book the author has written some modified rules, which he has come across during 
his practical studies, for those who are well versed with the sidereal and tropical and KP but 
not for the KP beginners. 


In judging the significance of twelve houses, the sub lord position is more important than its 
star lord. It is explained like this; in twin horoscopes the star lord’s position can remain the 
same while the sub positions are different for both the charts; this difference gives a more 
clear picture of the charts. It is also said that for the correct intensity of results, 1) judge the 
cusp sub lord’s significance and in which house the sub lord of the house under considera- 
tion is deposited, and 2) judge the cusp sub lord’s significance and in which house, the star 
lord of the sub lord of that house which is under consideration is deposited. (Part I pp 2-5) 
The author’s practice of using the horary numbers beyond 249 is explained. In addition to 
the Hindu rasi to rasi aspects, the Western aspects are also recommended. 

In matching the horoscopes, the following points in an individual chart are mentioned to be 
considered: 


1. Longevity, 

2. Health- physically and mentally, 

3. Promise of married life, 

4. Status of the married life, 

5. Promise of the child, 

6. Financial aspects, 

7. Dasa and progression after marriage. 


KP Ezine Februarv 2014 62 


Regarding the remedy, it is said that among the three types of karma, namely Dhruda Kar- 
ma, Dhruda Adhruda Karma and Adhruda Karma, in Dhruda Karma there is no escapism 
from the results, whether one can perform any remedy or not. In the other two types of kar- 
ma, the remedy can give some relief, if it’s mentioned in the chart. (Part I p 25) 


In judging the planet, the author has mentioned that the planet is to perform three roles 
as: 

1. The planet itself; 

2. The star lord of the planet; 

3. The sub lord of the planet. 


In the first condition the planet becomes the source for the star lord’s matter. In the second 
condition the planet represents the mater. In the third condition the planet shows positive 
or negative result of the star lord i.e. matter. When a planet does not become the star lord 
of any planet, the planet itself gives the result according to it’s natural and radical position, 
and not necessarily to judge the sub lord of the planet. (Part I p 34) 

It can be compared with the rule that if no planet is in the stars of a planet, that planet be- 
comes the strong significator of the houses for which it is the cuspal sub lord. 


In the author’s view one should restrict up to the sub lord (3"4 step) of the planet. If the star 
lord of the sub lord (46 step) is further considered, it increases the double probability of the 
result. So it is not a correct approach. (Part I p 36) 


The rectification of birth time is explained by using the original five ruling planets i.e. the 
asc. sign lord and star lord, Moon’s sign lord and star lord, and the day lord. Rahu or Ketu 
is considered if it represents any RP. 


In the Part II of the “Nakshatra Chintan”, thirty example charts, most of these known na- 
tives like Mhatma Gandhiji, Uttam Kumar, Lata Mangeshkar, Mujiber Rehman, Vijay Mer- 
chant, Zulfikar Bhutto, John F. Kennedy, Morarji Desai, Acharya Rajneesh, Sanjay Gandhi 
etc. and other known charts from Shri Chandrakant Bhatt’s publications with his kind per- 
mission. Each chart has been analyzed by using the K.P. rules and the author’s new sug- 
gested a Common Joint Rulers Theory “CJRT”, which is an application of some yoga theory 
of nirayana and sayana systems in the K.P. system. Before explaining his CJRT the author 
has clearly said that except Punarphoo yoga, late Shri K.S. Krishnamurthy has not consid- 
ered a single yoga from any other system. (Part II p 67) 


As said by the author in the preface of Part II, this book is neither for the beginners nor for 
those who have not studied K.P. properly.

Is President Barack Obama Having an Affair With Beyonce? French Media Think So 
By Keerthi Mohan: Subscribe to Keerthi’s RSS feed | February 11, 2014 12:45 PM IST 


If speculations are true, U.S. President Barack Obama’s marriage might be on the rocks, and 
he is believed to be growing distant from his wife, Michelle. 

The French media on Monday took note of this alleged trouble in Obama’s marriage and 
claimed that he might be cheating on his wife with singer Beyonce. 

Comments on the affair were first made on Europe 1 radio station on Monday morning, Mail 
Online reported, adding that Pascal Rostain, the photographer who took pictures of French 
president Francois Hollande secretly visiting his lover, spoke of the Obama-Beyonce affair. 
“You know, at this moment, in the United States, there’s something huge which is about to 
happen,” Rostain told interviewer Jean-Marc Morandini, according to Mail Online. 

“Indeed, it will come out tomorrow in the Washington Post. We cannot say that it is from 
the gutter press - a supposed liaison between President Barack Obama and Beyonce. I can 
assure you that the world will talk.”

Foreign assignment 


By: Er. V.K Sharma, B.E. (Elect), 
JYOTISHVID (PRASHER), K.P HORARATNA 
Superintending Engineer (Retired.), 
Punjab State Electricity Board, 
Address: #104, City Enclave, Zirakpur, 
Mohali (Chandigarh). 
Cell — 09417117370, e-mail: nickKO885@gmail.com 





A querent who was working in a M.N.C. in Gurgoan was anxious to obtain foreign assign- 
ment for the last 2 to 3 years but was not able to get the same in spite of continuous ef- 
forts and stiff competition from fellow employees. She along with her husband approached 
me to check astrologically when she will proceed on foreign assignment. I told her to inti- 
mate any horary number between 1 and 249. She told the number 15. So I cast the horary 
chart for the said number. 


NUMBER GIVEN BY THE CONSULTANT: 15 


PLACE OF JUDGEMENT: CHANDIGARH 
DATE OF JUDGEMENT: 25-4-2013 
TIME OF JUDGEMENT: 11:44 AM 


Moon reveals the nature of query. 

Moon is in 6, in star of Mars in 12, lord of 1 and 8, and is in the sub of Venus in 12, lord 
of 2. Hence Moon is linked with 12 [stay in foreign country], 6 [job], 2 [financial gain] and 
8[tension]. So Moon reveals the true nature of query that the querent was under tension 
for not getting foreign assignment. 


Gulbarga theory 

As per Gulbarga theory, if Ascendant sub lord of horary number furnished happens to be 
either Moon star lord or lagna sub lord of Ruling Planets, then answer to the query is af- 
firmative, otherwise not. In the case under reference, Ascendant sub lord is Mars and 
Moon star lord is also Mars. Hence the answer to the query is affirmative. Accordingly, I 
told the querent that she would get foreign assignment as desired. 


RULING PLANETS OF DATED 25-4-2013 AT 11:44 AM AT CHANDIGARH 


ASC SIGN LORD: MOON 
MOON STAR LORD: MARS 
MOON SIGN LORD: VENUS 
DAY LORD: JUPITER 


Rule for going abroad 

As per Horary Astrology 6 reader written by Sh K.S. Krishnamurti on page 301, for going 
abroad one is to judge the 12th cusp, and find out whether the sub lord of the 12th cusp 
is either retrograde or deposited in a constellation whose lord is retrograde. If either is ret- 
rograde one cannot go abroad. If the sub lord and lord of the constellation in which the 
sub lord is situated are in direct motion and if the sub lord of the 12th cusp is also a sig- 
nificator of either 3rd or 9th or 12th house one goes abroad. 


12th Cusp Sub Lord 

In this case 12th cusp sub lord is Venus in 12, lord of 2 and 7; it is in the star of own and 
in the sub of Rahu in 7. Rahu is conjoined with Saturn in 6, lord of 10 and 11, and Saturn 
aspects 9. Hence 12‘ cusp sub lord and its star lord are not retrograde, and it signifies 9 
and 12. So it fulfills the necessary condition for foreign travel. Further 12th cusp sub lord 
is also the significator of 6,10 and 11. So the querent will go abroad for job. For timing it is 
to check Mahdasha, Bhukti and Antra dasha period.

Identifying a Great Lover 


In looking at the charts of great lovers we have to start with the chart of Giacomo Casanova 
who is synonymous seducer. In his 5th house of sexual activity for fun, Casanova has Sun, 
the planet of casual sex or recreational sex, Mars, the ruler of 7" house and physical energy 
part of sex, Mercury, ruler of the intellect and rational mind, and Ascendant and 8 lord 
Venus, ruler of the passion and emotional part of sex, which further reinforces her role in 
the area of sex and entertainment. All these Sun, Mars, Mercury and 5 cusp are placed in 
Pisces, which is the sign associated with intemperance and a craving for emotional excite- 
ment and sensuality. Mars-Jupiter conjunction indicates his rebellious nature, exceptional 
sex life in the way against the moral code of their time and a large number of sexual con- 
quests. Promiscuous behavior is also associated with Saturn’s aspect on Venus. Neptune in 
the 8 house triggers a special fondness for experiencing sexuality in a spiritual way. Jupi- 
ter’s aspect on the Ascendant-Uranus conjunction adds charisma. However the Uranus- 
Rahu conjunction in the first house could explain some of his more unusual tastes of hav- 
ing liaisons with under age young girls. 


The predominant 5th house and 5 and 7‘ cuspal sub lord (CSL) Saturn’s signification of 
houses 5, 11 made him irresistible, sure of himself, and sexually attractive. 1, 5, 7, 9 and 
11% houses are connected by being in the same sub lord of Saturn. The 5th house is also 
relevant to other areas of Casanova's life as he was also known to be a consummate gam- 
bler. The 10» CSL Ketu also signifies 5t* house, and is connected with Jupiter and Venus. 
Casanova was trained for the priesthood, later was an obsessive gambler and a scholar at 
various stages of his life. Sun, Mercury and Venus, all in Pisces, is the sensual, romantic, 
artistic, and occult side of Casanova. 


Wanderings 


The Ist, 5th , 7th | 9th and 11% cuspal sub lord (CSL) Saturn is in house 3, lord of houses 
4,5, in the star of Sun in house 6, lord of Badhaka house 11 and in the sub of Jupiter in 
house 4, lord of houses 3, 6. 


The 34, 4th and 12th CSL Mercury is in house 5, lord of houses 9,12, in the star of Saturn 
in house 3, lord of houses 4,5 and sub of Venus in house 5, lord of houses 1,8. 


The 1st and 9 CSL Saturn’s signification of house 3, the 3™4 and 128 CSL Mercury’s signifi- 


cation of houses 3,9,12, and connection of 3,9,12t significators to each other gave him 
restless wanderings throughout Europe in Italy, France, Germany, Austria, England, Swit-

zerland, Belgium, Russia, Poland, Spain, Holland, Turkey. The metropolises Paris, London, 
Rome, Madrid, Vienna, Dresden, Berlin, Prague Warsaw, Moscow and St. Petersburg were 
Casanova’s stopping points, among others, after 1757. Gambling debts and erotic intrigues 
however forced Casanova to constantly and quickly change his location. 


Casanova finally settled down abroad at Duchcov (now in Czech Republic) as librarian for 
the Bohemian Count Waldstein. The 11 (reunion with his kith and kin) signification is 
missing to return to mother land. In the wandering the 34, 4th and 12 houses are connect- 
ed by being in the same sub of dual planet Mercury. Further duality is also involved; 9th 
cusp is in dual sign Gemini, and 3 cusp is in another dual sign Sagittarius; 9t* CSL Saturn 
is in the star of Sun in dual sign Pisces, and 3 and 12 CSL is a dual planet Mercury lo- 
cated in Pisces together with Mercury’s sub Venus. 


In his long, wild, and scandalous life, h also met famous contemporaries such as Voltaire, 
the Chevalier d'Eon, Benjamin Franklin, Jean-Jacques Rousseau, Mozart, Louis XV, George 
II, Friedrich the Great of Prussia, Catherine the Great of Russia, and Pope Clement XIII. 


Duel Fight 


The Mars, god of war and sex, and bravery, in 5‘ (house of love affairs and risk), the 3™ CSL 
Mercury’s signification of 3™4 house, and the Uranus-Ascendant conjunction made Casanova 
a risk taker to fight duals with courage. 


The most deadly encounter was the dual with Polish general Branicki at Warsaw on 5 
March 1766 (Su-Mo-Ju-Ke). Casanova was obliged to challenge Branicki to a duel over an 
Branicki’s insult caused by a ballet actress in whom neither he nor his Polish rival had the 
slightest interest. They fought the duel with pistols as Branicki wanted. Branicki was se- 
verely wounded with shrapnel in his stomach. Casanova was slightly wounded in the skin 
of the left arm. The signification of life saving 5t4 house by Dasa lord Sun and 1*t, 5 houses 
by Bhukti- Antra- Sookshma lords saved Casanova’s life. Casanova’s duel with Branicki at- 
tracted a great deal of attention all over Europe. Casanova had remained proud of this epi- 
sode for the rest of his life by creating a work of thrilling adventure and inimitable literary 
style. 


Imprisonment 


The 12» CSL Mercury’s signification of houses 3,8,12 and connection to Saturn indicates 
imprisonment many times in his life. The worst one was on 26 Jul 1755 when he was was 
condemned to five years imprisonment without trial. That happened during Dasa Venus 
(signifiators of houses 2,3,8), Bhukti Rahu (2,8), Antra Moon (2,8,12) and Sookshma Mercu- 
ry (3,8,12). 


Fifteen months later came Casanova’s legendary escape from the lead chambers in Venice. 
Forced into exile, Casanova led from now on an even more nomadic, varied life that would 
give him material for his stories. In Paris he was admitted to the most exclusive circles and 
appointed director of the French lottery. His interest the occult and black magic fascinated 
women of high rank, amongst them the Marquise d'Urfe, who supported him lavishly for 
many years. 


Denial of Marriage 


On the long list of the 122 hearts he conquered, Casanova wrote the names of many well- 
known European women of his time. Although he was nearly married on two occasions it 
was not materialized due to the 7 CSL Saturn’s strong signification of marriage denial 
house 6 (12 to 7), and missing signification of house 2 (maintaining the family) and house 
7 (legal bondage by marriage), but only affair by affair was going on by signification of hous-

The 10% cusp, 10 CSL Ketut, and its star lord Rahu are all located in movable signs, i.e.

officer, violinist, con man, pimp, gourmand, dancer, businessman, diplomat, spy, politi- 
cian, mathematician, social philosopher, cabalist, playwright, and writer. 


The 10% (name, fame) CSL Ketu is the strong significator of house 10 as Ketu is the CSL of

This Ketu also signifies the 4th, house of one's legacy and what one leaves behind after

with my life partner (wife)?
